cost_model_summary: Summary of recommended reserved capacity economics: propose 12-month base commit with optional 36-month discount tier. Pilot: reserve 8 A100-80GB equiv GPUs (reserved pool), 3-month ramp. Production target: 24 GPUs reserved for steady-state. Utilization assumptions: conservative 40% during ramp, base-case 65% steady state, aggressive 85% with batching and cache. Unit economics (model): at 65% util -> ~$0.00095 per token (approx $0.95 / 1k tokens); at 85% util w/ KV-cache & batching -> ~$0.00065/token. Break-even vs in-house capex: ~60% sustained utilization for 12-24 month horizon. Include burst bucket for on-demand excess at higher per-token pricing. Notes on drivers: GPU type, sequence length distribution, batching efficiency, KV cache hit-rate, and network egress impact per-request latency/cost.
throughput_guarantees_and_slos: Throughput targets discussed: sustain 250-300 concurrent user sessions with 100 qps baseline per pool; Redwood to provide per-route throughput metrics and throttling policies. SLO asks: p95 <= 250ms (short chat), p99 <= 500ms (end-to-end on VPC peering). Requested automated fallback policy to lower-cost model variant on overload. Proposed SLA credits: graded by p99 miss% with remediation credits and operational remediation windows.
reserved_capacity_plan: Proposed reserved plan: Phase 1 (pilot): 8 reserved GPUs for 3 months. Phase 2 (prod): 24 reserved GPUs with autoscale headroom + burst pool (shared across regions). Suggested partitioning: dedicate 60% capacity to operator-assist (low-latency), 30% to batch embedding jobs (scheduled off-peak), 10% for canary/QA. Include autoscale policy for daytime peaks and offload to private dev capacity for nightly batches. Financials: show per-GPU monthly cost, effective tokens/hour capacity, and blended per-token cost at different utilizations.
procurement_notes: Procurement is evaluating 12-month vs 36-month commit. CFO requested ARR impact model, op-ex vs cap-ex comparison, and cancellation terms. Legal requested explicit SLA draft; security requires SOC2 + ISO attestation before go-live. Capital sign-off path: CTO -> Head of Ops -> CFO. Decision criteria: meets p99 SLA in production POC, cost advantage vs in-house at target utilization, clean peering terms.
